precision-references.title: Choose a shunt resistor
precision-references.prompt: A 2.048 V shunt needs 150 μA, the load needs 80 μA, and supply ranges from 2.7 to 3.3 V. Find the maximum feed resistance and the high-supply no-load reference current for 2.7 kΩ.
precision-references.hint: Use minimum supply for the current guarantee; maximum supply with no load for stress.

solution.text: The upper resistance is (2.7 − 2.048)/230 μA = 2.835 kΩ. At 3.3 V a 2.7 kΩ feed supplies 463.7 μA. Check resistor tolerance, reference voltage tolerance and maximum permitted current.

precision-references.title: Reference drift in codes
precision-references.prompt: A 12-bit ADC uses 2.5 V. The reference changes by +60 ppm while a fixed input is at 75% of nominal span. Estimate the code change.
precision-references.hint: Reference error scales the code with the opposite sign.

solution.text: Nominal code is approximately 3072; its change is −3072 × 60 ppm = −0.1843 code. The input-referred voltage error is −112.5 μV. The digital output may or may not change by one code depending on its distance to a transition.

precision-references.title: Size a first-pass reservoir
precision-references.prompt: A reference charge impulse is 80 pC. What ideal capacitance limits its immediate droop to 20 μV? Why is this not a complete design?
precision-references.hint: Use charge conservation before adding the drive impedance.

solution.text: C ≥ 80 pC / 20 μV = 4 μF. Check effective capacitance under bias, ESR/ESL, recovery before the next conversion and reference-buffer stability. An ideal capacitor-only calculation omits those constraints.

precision-noise-grounding.title: Integrate a real low-pass
precision-noise-grounding.prompt: A flat 8 nV/√Hz density passes through a unity first-order 200 Hz low-pass. Find rms noise.
precision-noise-grounding.hint: Its noise bandwidth is larger than its −3 dB bandwidth.

solution.text: The equivalent bandwidth is π × 200 / 2 = 314.16 Hz. Noise is 8 × √314.16 = 141.8 nV rms.

precision-noise-grounding.title: A fast shared inductance
precision-noise-grounding.prompt: A 20 nH common return carries a current that rises by 0.25 A in 25 ns. Find the induced voltage.
precision-noise-grounding.hint: Use di/dt, not switching repetition frequency.

solution.text: 20 nH × 0.25 A / 25 ns = 0.2 V. Its effect depends on which sensitive terminals share this path; reduce loop/shared inductance.

precision-noise-grounding.title: Leakage in a current measurement
precision-noise-grounding.prompt: A 1 TΩ path from 3 V to a virtual-ground input feeds a 10 GΩ feedback resistor. Calculate output error; repeat with a guard at 3 mV.
precision-noise-grounding.hint: The guard changes voltage across the unwanted insulation.

solution.text: Ungarded leakage is 3 pA, giving 30 mV magnitude. With 3 mV across the same insulation, leakage is 3 fA and output error 30 μV. Guard-driver leakage and noise must also be budgeted.

precision-calibration.title: Invert a measured line
precision-calibration.prompt: At 0.1 V a meter reads 2100 counts; at 2.1 V it reads 42100 counts. What corrected voltage corresponds to 17100 counts?
precision-calibration.hint: Fit slope and intercept, then invert.

solution.text: Slope is 20000 counts/V. Intercept is 100 counts. The corrected result is (17100 − 100)/20000 = 0.850 V.

precision-calibration.title: Choose excitation current
precision-calibration.prompt: A 1000 Ω sensor must dissipate no more than 0.05 mW. What current limit follows?
precision-calibration.hint: Power depends on the square of current.

solution.text: I ≤ √(0.05 mW / 1000 Ω) = 223.6 μA. Check resistance at the hottest operating point and the sensor’s thermal mounting.

precision-calibration.title: Separate sensor and thermal EMF
precision-calibration.prompt: A resistor measured at ±0.5 mA gives +50.007 mV and −49.993 mV. Find resistance and additive EMF.
precision-calibration.hint: Difference isolates the odd component; sum isolates the even component.

solution.text: Resistance is 100.000 Ω from 100.000 mV / 1 mA. Additive EMF is 7 μV. This assumes equal current magnitude and no drift between readings.

power-linear-regulators.title: Can a current-rated LDO survive?
power-linear-regulators.prompt: A 9-to-3.3 V LDO delivers 0.3 A at 45 °C ambient. Assume 50 K/W and ignore quiescent loss. Estimate junction temperature.
power-linear-regulators.hint: Use the voltage difference, not output power, for pass loss.

solution.text: Loss is 5.7 × 0.3 = 1.71 W. Estimated junction is 45 + 50 × 1.71 = 130.5 °C. Compare to the guaranteed operating limit and actual board thermal performance; a current rating alone does not qualify this case.

power-linear-regulators.title: Bound a load-step capacitor
power-linear-regulators.prompt: A 0.2 A increase must cause less than 40 mV droop before a 5 μs response. Ignore ESR first. What effective capacitance is required?

solution.text: C ≥ 0.2 × 5 μs / 0.04 = 25 μF. Add ESR/ESL error, tolerance and DC-bias derating; nominal 25 μF may be insufficient.

power-linear-regulators.title: Separate rejection from generated noise
power-linear-regulators.prompt: A 50 mV rms ripple lies at a frequency where PSRR is 40 dB. The LDO generates 300 μV rms independent noise in the measured band. Find combined rms.
power-linear-regulators.hint: Attenuate the ripple, then sum independent powers.

solution.text: Ripple becomes 500 μV rms. Combined magnitude is √(500² + 300²) = 583.1 μV rms. The uncorrelated assumption and actual PSRR conditions must hold.

power-buck-converters.title: Choose the inductor
power-buck-converters.prompt: Design an ideal 24-to-6 V buck at 400 kHz for 0.4 A peak-to-peak ripple. Find L and the CCM boundary.
power-buck-converters.hint: First derive duty, then use the rising ramp.

solution.text: D = 0.25; L = (24 − 6) × 0.25 / (400 kHz × 0.4 A) = 28.125 μH. The boundary load is 0.2 A. Verify peak current and controller minimum on-time.

power-buck-converters.title: Find the capacitor stress
power-buck-converters.prompt: A buck supplies 2 A at duty 0.3 with small inductor ripple. What are average input current and input-capacitor rms current?
power-buck-converters.hint: Average source current and pulsed capacitor current are different.

solution.text: Average input is 0.6 A. Capacitor rms is 2√(0.3 × 0.7) = 0.9165 A. Check ripple-current rating, ESR heating and local loop inductance.

power-buck-converters.title: Test a low-load waveform
power-buck-converters.prompt: A diode buck has 0.6 A ripple and supplies 0.1 A. Is a waveform with −0.2 A valley physical?
power-buck-converters.hint: Check what can conduct reverse current.

solution.text: No: the CCM expression gives a negative valley but the diode stage enters DCM when current reaches zero. A forced-continuous synchronous converter can support reversal, but it is a different operating mode.

power-boost-isolated.title: A boost current rating
power-boost-isolated.prompt: A 3-to-9 V ideal boost supplies 0.3 A with 0.4 A ripple. Find duty, average inductor current and peak.
power-boost-isolated.hint: Only the off interval supplies the output.

solution.text: D = 2/3, average current = 0.3/(1/3) = 0.9 A, peak = 1.1 A. Real efficiency and current-limit tolerances increase the required margin.

power-boost-isolated.title: Find negative-rail stress
power-boost-isolated.prompt: An ideal inverting buck–boost makes −12 V from +5 V. Find duty and approximate switch blocking voltage.
power-boost-isolated.hint: The inductor transfers to the output in a separate interval.

solution.text: D = 12/17 = 0.7059. Ideal blocking voltage is 17 V. Add switching overshoot and derating; check controller pin reference voltages.

power-boost-isolated.title: A DCM flyback power estimate
power-boost-isolated.prompt: A flyback has 80 μH magnetizing inductance, 0.8 A peak current and 100 kHz switching. Estimate ideal power and output at 85% efficiency.
power-boost-isolated.hint: Each fully demagnetized cycle transfers one stored-energy packet.

solution.text: Energy per cycle is 25.6 μJ, giving 2.56 W ideal and 2.176 W at the assumed efficiency. Verify complete demagnetization, core flux and peak current.

power-control-layout.title: Test a sampled current loop
power-control-layout.prompt: An ideal peak-current loop has m₁ = 0.1 A/μs and m₂ = 0.3 A/μs. Find the minimum compensation slope for stability and the multiplier at mₐ = 0.2 A/μs.

solution.text: The strict stability condition is mₐ > 0.1 A/μs. At 0.2 A/μs, λ = (0.2 − 0.3)/(0.1 + 0.2) = −1/3. Perturbations alternate and shrink in this ideal model.

power-control-layout.title: A capacitor eats the current budget
power-control-layout.prompt: A 470 μF output ramps to 3.3 V in 3 ms. The normal load draws 0.2 A. Estimate required current during the linear ramp.
power-control-layout.hint: Add capacitor current and load current.

solution.text: Capacitor current is 0.517 A; total is 0.717 A. Include load dependence on voltage, tolerance and converter current-limit behavior.

power-control-layout.title: Locate a ringing frequency
power-control-layout.prompt: A switching loop has 20 nH and 500 pF equivalent capacitance. Estimate resonance and characteristic impedance.

solution.text: Frequency is 50.33 MHz; impedance is 6.325 Ω. These are model scales, not a complete RC-snubber prescription.

rf-impedance-matching.title: Translate a measured sine
rf-impedance-matching.prompt: A 0.4 V peak sine drives 50 Ω. Find power and dBm.

rf-impedance-matching.title: Design a resistance transformation
rf-impedance-matching.prompt: Match a 25 Ω source to 100 Ω at 1 MHz using series L and shunt C on the load.
rf-impedance-matching.hint: Derive Q, then series and shunt reactances.

solution.text: Q = √3; Xs = 43.30 Ω, |Xp| = 57.735 Ω. L = 6.892 μH and C = 2.757 nF. Verify the parallel branch is 25 − j43.30 Ω.

rf-impedance-matching.title: Interpret a return-loss claim
rf-impedance-matching.prompt: A port has 20 dB return loss at one frequency. Find reflection magnitude and reflected power fraction.
rf-impedance-matching.hint: Use amplitude dB for Γ, then square it.

solution.text: |Γ| = 0.1; reflected power is 1%. This specifies a match at that condition, not insertion loss or broadband performance.

rf-signal-chains.title: Estimate a receiver floor
rf-signal-chains.prompt: At 290 K, a receiver has 3 dB NF, 20 kHz noise bandwidth and needs 12 dB SNR. Estimate sensitivity without processing gain.
rf-signal-chains.hint: Start with −174 dBm/Hz and add bandwidth, NF and required SNR.

solution.text: −174 + 10 log₁₀(20000) + 3 + 12 = −115.99 dBm. Filter noise bandwidth and modulation/detection assumptions must be specified.

rf-signal-chains.title: Find the unwanted input
rf-signal-chains.prompt: Desired RF is 125 MHz, LO is 110 MHz and a real mixer selects 15 MHz IF. Find the image.
rf-signal-chains.hint: Both signs of RF minus LO give the same real IF.

solution.text: 95 MHz also converts to 15 MHz. Reject it before mixing or use a calibrated quadrature/image-reject architecture.

rf-signal-chains.title: Two tones meet an intercept
rf-signal-chains.prompt: An amplifier has 15 dB gain and +5 dBm IIP3. Each input tone is −25 dBm. Estimate fundamental and IM3 output.
rf-signal-chains.hint: Use linear and cubic dB slopes separately.

solution.text: Fundamental is −10 dBm; IM3 is 3(−25)+15−2(5) = −70 dBm, or 60 dBc below each tone. This is a small-signal intercept estimate.

transmission-lines.title: A slow clock with fast edges
transmission-lines.prompt: A 15 cm line has velocity 1.5 × 10⁸ m/s and carries a 2 MHz clock with 0.8 ns edges. Find flight time and the relevant timescale.
transmission-lines.hint: Compare flight time with edge time.

solution.text: Flight is 1 ns, comparable to the 0.8 ns edge. Use a transmission-line model despite the 500 ns repetition period.

transmission-lines.title: A nonmatched load
transmission-lines.prompt: A 2 V source with 50 Ω resistance drives a 50 Ω line into 150 Ω. Find launch, reflection and first load voltage.
transmission-lines.hint: Use the source-to-line divider before the load arrives.

solution.text: Launch is 1 V, ΓL = 0.5 and first load voltage is 1.5 V. The matched source absorbs the return; final DC is also 1.5 V.

transmission-lines.title: Locate a discontinuity
transmission-lines.prompt: A TDR sees a reflection 4 ns after launch on a line with velocity 1.6 × 10⁸ m/s. Find distance.

solution.text: Distance is 0.32 m from the calibrated reference plane.

differential-pairs.title: Translate a differential swing
differential-pairs.prompt: A pair has 1.2 V common mode and +0.6 V differential voltage. Find the two conductor voltages.
differential-pairs.hint: Split differential voltage equally around the common value.

solution.text: The plus conductor is 1.5 V and minus conductor is 0.9 V. Check each pin’s allowed common-mode and absolute voltage range.

differential-pairs.title: A timing mismatch becomes common mode
differential-pairs.prompt: Each conductor transitions by 0.5 V in 0.8 ns. One is delayed 80 ps. Estimate transient common-mode excursion for linear ramps.
differential-pairs.hint: Use half the single-ended transition times the fractional skew.

solution.text: Excursion is 0.5/2 × 0.08/0.8 = 25 mV. This assumes equal shapes and skew smaller than rise time.

differential-pairs.title: Allocate an electrical-length budget
differential-pairs.prompt: A channel allows 25 ps intrapair skew and propagation velocity is 160 mm/ns. Find the length difference budget and name other contributors.
differential-pairs.hint: Convert time to distance, then budget packages and connectors too.

solution.text: Length difference is 4 mm if all skew is assigned to PCB traces. Package, connector, via and material asymmetry consume part of the same timing budget.

sampling-converter-errors.title: Bins and ideal noise
sampling-converter-errors.prompt: A 14-bit converter has a 4 V span. Find bin width and ideal rms quantization noise.

solution.text: q = 244.14 μV; q/√12 = 70.477 μV rms under the uncorrelated uniform-error model.

sampling-converter-errors.title: A blocker survives software filtering
sampling-converter-errors.prompt: A 13 kHz input is sampled at 12 kS/s. Find its first-zone alias and explain whether a 2 kHz digital low-pass removes it.
sampling-converter-errors.hint: Find the distance to a multiple of the sample rate.

solution.text: It aliases to 1 kHz and passes the 2 kHz low-pass. Attenuate the original 13 kHz input before sampling.

sampling-converter-errors.title: Budget a source resistance
sampling-converter-errors.prompt: A 16-bit ADC uses 30 pF sampling capacitance and 300 ns acquisition. Find the maximum R in the ideal full-span first-order model.

solution.text: R ≤ 300 ns / [17 ln2 × 30 pF] = 848.65 Ω. Real driver settling and switch resistance consume part of this budget.

adc-successive-approximation.title: Trace five trial bits
adc-successive-approximation.prompt: For an ideal 5-bit SAR with 1 V reference and input 0.43 V, determine the trials and result under the floor-bin convention.
adc-successive-approximation.hint: Start at half scale and keep a bit only if its trial does not exceed input.

solution.text: Trials are 0.5 reject, 0.25 keep, 0.375 keep, 0.4375 reject, 0.40625 keep. Code is 01101 = 13, bin [0.40625, 0.4375) V.

adc-successive-approximation.title: Conversion charge and droop
adc-successive-approximation.prompt: A SAR draws an 80 pC reference packet at 500 kS/s from 2.2 μF effective capacitance. Find average current and immediate ideal droop.
adc-successive-approximation.hint: Average demand and impulse response are different.

solution.text: Average current is 40 μA; droop is 36.36 μV. Recovery, ESR/ESL and code dependence still need verification.

adc-successive-approximation.title: A serial link limits throughput
adc-successive-approximation.prompt: An ADC transaction uses 16 result bits plus 8 status bits. A 12 MHz serial clock supports no overlap and 0.5 μs overhead. Find maximum transaction rate.
adc-successive-approximation.hint: Include the bits and the gap.

solution.text: Clocking takes 24/12 MHz = 2 μs. Total is 2.5 μs, allowing 400 ktransactions/s before conversion/acquisition constraints.

adc-flash-pipeline.title: Comparator growth
adc-flash-pipeline.prompt: How many ideal full-flash comparators are required for 6 bits and 10 bits?
adc-flash-pipeline.hint: Every internal threshold needs a comparison.

solution.text: Counts are 63 and 1023. The ratio is about 16.24, illustrating exponential hardware growth.

adc-flash-pipeline.title: A redundant stage stays reversible
adc-flash-pipeline.prompt: For normalized input x = −0.4, compute the ideal 1.5-bit decision and residue, then reconstruct x.
adc-flash-pipeline.hint: Use thresholds at ±0.25 and r = 2x − d.

solution.text: Decision is d = −1; residue is 0.2. Reconstruction (−1 + 0.2)/2 gives −0.4. The residue is within [−1,1].

adc-flash-pipeline.title: Rate is not immediate response
adc-flash-pipeline.prompt: A 125 MS/s ADC has eight sample-clock cycles of latency. Find latency and sample spacing.
adc-flash-pipeline.hint: Both quantities use the same clock but different cycle counts.

solution.text: Spacing is 8 ns; pipeline latency is 64 ns before output-link and processing delays.

adc-integrating-delta-sigma.title: Cancel integrator values
adc-integrating-delta-sigma.prompt: An integrating ADC uses 80 ms input integration and a 2.5 V reference; rundown lasts 24 ms. Find the constant input voltage.

solution.text: Input is 2.5 × 24/80 = 0.75 V. Ideal R, C and common clock frequency cancel; unequal phase errors do not.

adc-integrating-delta-sigma.title: Interpret a one-bit stream
adc-integrating-delta-sigma.prompt: A normalized ±1 feedback stream contains 700 positive decisions and 300 negative decisions. What input average does ideal bounded charge balance indicate?
adc-integrating-delta-sigma.hint: Average the actual feedback levels, not the unsigned bits alone.

solution.text: Mean is (700 − 300)/1000 = 0.4. Finite residual state gives a bounded correction; the 0.7 ones fraction is not the signed input.

adc-integrating-delta-sigma.title: A sinc filter is not instantaneous
adc-integrating-delta-sigma.prompt: A sinc³ teaching decimator has modulator clock 128 kHz and M = 128. Find output rate and group delay.
adc-integrating-delta-sigma.hint: Use three boxcar delays at modulator rate.

solution.text: Output is 1 kS/s; delay is 3 × 127/(2 × 128000) = 1.4883 ms. Step settling is longer than group delay and additional internal stages may add latency.

dac-architectures-output.title: Maximum code is below reference
dac-architectures-output.prompt: A 10-bit ideal DAC has 2.048 V reference and denominator 2ᴺ. Find the step, output at code 700 and output at maximum code.
dac-architectures-output.hint: There are 1024 code weights but maximum unsigned code is 1023.

solution.text: Step is 2 mV; code 700 gives 1.400 V; code 1023 gives 2.046 V.

dac-architectures-output.title: A major carry exposes mismatch
dac-architectures-output.prompt: An 8-bit weighted-current DAC has ideal lower-bit sum 127 units, but its MSB is 126.8 units. What happens from code 127 to 128?
dac-architectures-output.hint: Compare sums before and after the carry.

solution.text: Output falls by 0.2 unit. DNL at that transition is −1.2 under the ideal one-unit step definition, so it is nonmonotonic.

dac-architectures-output.title: Carrier, resolution and ripple
dac-architectures-output.prompt: A 100 MHz timer uses 10-bit PWM and 1 ms RC. At 3.3 V half duty, estimate carrier and ripple.
dac-architectures-output.hint: The period has 1024 counts; use the small-ripple RC expression.

solution.text: Carrier is 97.656 kHz. Ripple is about 3.3 × 0.25/(97656 × 0.001) = 8.448 mV. Effective output precision also depends on supply/reference and settling.
